company.snapshot: AgileMind is a Grapevine, Texas-based educational technology company founded in 2002 that develops research-based mathematics and science curriculum programs (grades 6–12) for U.S. school districts. Their blended learning model combines print student activity books (SABs) with digital instructional platforms; products are sold on annual contracts to districts and carry regional ISBNs that vary by state. AgileMind was acquired by Savvas Learning Company in 2020 and operates with approximately 51–100 employees.

businessObjects: Contacts (district administrators, principals, teachers — Salesforce Contact)
Products / Titles (curriculum book series, e.g. Intensified Algebra Vol 1 — Salesforce Product + QB Item)
ISBNs (regional identifiers per product × state — Salesforce configurable lookup table)
Inventory Records (quantities on hand, committed, available per title — QB + Salesforce Inventory__c)

phase1.label: Connected
phase1.headline: Agreement-to-Invoice and Inventory in One View
phase1.body: The 4 confirmed flows close the manual gaps Crystal and Holly live in daily: UC1 fires when Abby creates an Agreement in Salesforce (Closed Won) and automatically creates the QuickBooks invoice — no manual re-entry. UC2 polls QuickBooks on a schedule and writes the invoice number, payment date, and open balance back to the Salesforce Agreement — Crystal stops toggling between systems. UC3 reads Holly's Google Sheets or Excel demand worksheet on a schedule and loads inventory quantities, committed stock, and projected shorts into a new Salesforce Inventory__c object. UC4 pulls QB inventory item costs into the same Salesforce object, so Maria can answer 'how much did we spend on Intensified Algebra Vol 1 over 5 years?' without leaving Salesforce.

phase2.label: Automated
phase2.headline: Shortage Alerts and Fulfillment Triggers Fire Themselves
phase2.body: With live inventory in Salesforce, automated rules become possible that aren't feasible today. When available inventory for a title drops below the configured 3% buffer (currently tracked manually in red on Holly's spreadsheet), Salesforce fires a shortage alert to Holly and the relevant sales rep automatically. When a district's pipeline stage crosses 60% probability, a pre-fulfillment reservation is triggered in QB — reducing the last-minute crunch at back-to-school. CCR fulfillment flags (UC6-potential) are stamped automatically on the incoming Agreement so the system knows materials were already shipped, eliminating Holly's manual reconciliation call to sales. Product catalog sync (UC5-potential) keeps QB items and Salesforce Products aligned so new title additions by Maria don't silently diverge from Abby's opportunity line items.

phase3.label: Agentic
phase3.headline: Agentforce Turns Salesforce Data Into District-Level Decisions
phase3.body: Phase 1 creates the Salesforce objects that Agentforce runs on: Agreement, Invoice status, Inventory__c, and Product. An Agentforce Sales Agent monitors open Agreements where the QB open balance has aged past 30 days and drafts a follow-up email to the district's finance contact — no action needed from Crystal. A second Agentforce agent answers Maria's natural-language procurement questions: 'What did we source for Intensified Algebra Vol 1 the last 3 fiscal years and what is left in inventory?' — pulling from the Inventory__c and Invoice history Phases 1–2 created. A third agent runs pre-season demand forecasting: reading open pipeline by probability stage from Opportunities, comparing against current QB inventory levels, and generating a draft purchase order recommendation for Holly's review — replacing the manual red-cell Excel exercise with a one-click approval workflow.

Platform Events or Change Data Capture must be enabled for Agreement object to support event-driven UC1 trigger

fieldKnowledgeCandidates.title: K-12 publisher regional ISBN complexity — state adoption drives per-state ISBN variants
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.trigger: AgileMind engagement — UC1 ISBN routing discovery
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.scenario: K-12 curriculum publishers who sell physical student activity books (SABs) to school districts assign distinct ISBNs per title × state. This is driven by state textbook adoption processes: 19 states plus DC make decisions at the state level, while the remainder delegate to local education agencies. Publishers adapt content per state (standards alignment, demographic content) and the ISBN reflects those variants. For an integration that routes fulfillment orders, the ISBN is not a static field — it is a function of (product, state, program year).
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.whatFailed: No automated ISBN resolution path at AgileMind — Abby manually reviews any order where the ISBN lookup table returns no match, creating a bottleneck during the back-to-school crunch.
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.whatWorked: Proposed solution: Salesforce custom metadata type or configurable lookup object (State × Product → ISBN), maintained by Sales Ops, queried at invoice creation time in the MuleSoft UC1 flow before QB invoice is generated.
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.clientQuestionUsed: What happens today when a district in a new state orders a title that hasn't been set up in your lookup table?
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.promotesTo: standards/playbooks/ as a K-12 publisher integration pattern note; candidate for FIELD_KNOWLEDGE.md FK entry

fieldKnowledgeCandidates.title: K-12 publisher fiscal year mismatch — publisher April 1 FY vs district June 30 FY creates seasonal AR pressure
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.trigger: AgileMind engagement — QB fiscal year April 1 confirmed in transcripts
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.scenario: K-12 curriculum publishers often run a fiscal year starting April 1 (aligned to their parent company or historical reporting cycles), while K-12 school district budgets almost universally run July 1 – June 30. This creates a structural lag: the publisher's Q4 (January–March) is the district's budget-planning season; the publisher's new fiscal year (April) opens while districts are still finalizing budgets and approving POs. The April–June window is simultaneously the publisher's Q1 and the district's year-end 'use it or lose it' spending crunch — creating a compressed billing and fulfillment window that hits both parties at the same time.
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.whatFailed: AgileMind's AR aging reports and inventory demand forecasts are misaligned with district purchasing timelines. Crystal and Holly are managing peak workflow manually in a 60-day window (May–July) with no automation.
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.whatWorked: Integration design must account for fiscal year offset in date-range queries: QB invoice date-range filters should use the publisher's April 1 FY, while Opportunity close-date filters and demand forecast horizon should use the district June 30 FY. Both ranges are needed to produce accurate pre-season forecasts.
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.clientQuestionUsed: Is your QuickBooks fiscal year April 1, and does your team track district budget approval cycles separately?
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.promotesTo: standards/playbooks/ as a K-12 publisher date-range integration pattern; candidate for FIELD_KNOWLEDGE.md FK entry

fieldKnowledgeCandidates.title: K-12 publisher back-to-school seasonality — 60-day order crunch compresses all fulfillment and billing into one window
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.trigger: AgileMind engagement — Holly's manual Excel workflow and shortage tracking
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.scenario: K-12 publishers experience a heavily compressed annual cycle. District budget approvals happen April–June; PO issuance and order confirmation happen May–July; materials must ship and be received before school starts (August). For print curriculum publishers, this means the majority of annual order volume — fulfillment, invoicing, inventory decrements, and AR — all hits within a 60-day window. Any manual process in this window is a failure risk. Publishers who haven't automated their order-to-invoice flow are most exposed during this period.
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.whatFailed: At AgileMind, Holly manually tracks inventory in a red-cell Excel spreadsheet during this window; Crystal manually creates and syncs QB invoices; no automated shortage alert exists. The risk of a stockout or missed invoice is highest precisely when there is no time to investigate.
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.whatWorked: The integration architecture (UC1–UC3) is deliberately designed to front-load the automation so that the August crunch becomes a monitoring exercise rather than a manual execution exercise. Phase 2 shortage alerts fire before the window, not during it.
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.clientQuestionUsed: What does your team's workload look like in May through July — is that the hardest window of the year operationally?
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.promotesTo: standards/scenarios/ as a seasonal-batch integration pattern note; candidate for FIELD_KNOWLEDGE.md FK entry

fieldKnowledgeCandidates.title: K-12 publisher invoicing — district PO timing and state funding cycles affect when invoices can legally be issued
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.scenario: School districts operate under state and federal funding rules that govern when purchase orders can be issued and when invoices can be accepted. In many states, invoices cannot be processed until a valid PO is in the system. The June 30 year-end creates a 'use it or lose it' dynamic: districts rush to obligate funds before fiscal year close, but the publisher cannot recognize the revenue until the invoice is accepted. For publishers automating invoice creation (UC1), the trigger should be confirmed Agreement/PO receipt — not just Opportunity Closed Won — or they risk creating invoices that districts cannot legally accept yet.
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.whatFailed: Not confirmed for AgileMind — this is a risk pattern, not a documented failure. The UC1 trigger design (Agreement Created in SF) should be validated against AgileMind's actual PO receipt workflow.
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.whatWorked: Recommended intake question: confirm whether AgileMind's Salesforce Agreement creation step already implies a received district PO, or whether there is a separate PO confirmation step before billing is appropriate.
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.clientQuestionUsed: When you create an Agreement in Salesforce — does that always mean you have a signed district PO in hand, or does the Agreement sometimes get created ahead of the PO?
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.promotesTo: standards/playbooks/ as a K-12 billing trigger pattern; candidate for FIELD_KNOWLEDGE.md FK entry

fieldKnowledgeCandidates.title: K-12 EdTech M&A integration risk — subsidiary systems diverge from parent after acquisition
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.trigger: AgileMind was acquired by Savvas Learning Company in 2020
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.scenario: When a K-12 EdTech or curriculum company is acquired, the subsidiary's operational systems (CRM, ERP, inventory) rarely get integrated with the parent in the first 3–5 years. The subsidiary continues to run their legacy tools while the parent pursues its own technology investments. This creates a window where the subsidiary's data is isolated — valuable for the parent's consolidated reporting but inaccessible without custom integration. AgileMind is 4 years post-acquisition and still running QuickBooks + Salesforce independently, with no evidence of Savvas-level ERP consolidation.
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.whatFailed: Post-acquisition integration neglect at AgileMind — the manual QB/SF workflow is a direct symptom of the subsidiary operating as a standalone since 2020.
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.whatWorked: DataSkate's integration work creates the data connective tissue that should have been built at acquisition. If Savvas eventually wants consolidated reporting, the Salesforce-centric architecture (Inventory__c, Agreement, Invoice sync) becomes the foundation for that rollup.
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.clientQuestionUsed: Has Savvas asked you to report inventory or billing data up to the parent level, or are you still operating fully independently?
fieldKnowledgeCandidates.promotesTo: standards/playbooks/ as an M&A integration pattern note; candidate for FIELD_KNOWLEDGE.md FK entry
